title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for clinical wellness visit classification in cats and dogs.
summary: Gradient boosting was trained on 11,105 veterinary visits from 655 animals across 544 practices; 400 expert-labeled visits drawn at random from the same database yielded specificity 0.94, sensitivity 0.86 and balanced accuracy 0.90. The annotation sample is not independent of the training data, and the authors themselves call for prospective validation. The result is visit classification; detection of subclinical disease is not established.
ai_technology: Specific veterinary visit classification result, but same-database expert sample limits independent validation; do not claim subclinical disease detection.
